AUTHOR: Pedersen
TITLE: Detection of Marine Animals in a New Underwater Dataset with Varying Visibility
SPECIES: Big fish (mostly lumpsucker, sculpin), small fish (mostly stickleback), crab, jellyfish, shrimp, starfish
DATA: Brackish Dataset (own footage; 89 clips, 14,518 frames, 25,613 annotations)
V_EV: Sec. 3: 'The setup is permanently mounted on a pillar of the Limfjords-bridge ... at a depth of around nine meters.'; Fig. 5 shows 'the variation in turbidity'
D_EV: Sec. 5.1: 'The dataset is split randomly into 80 % training, 10 % validation and 10 % test data.'
R_EV: Sec. 5.2: 'The networks have been evaluated on the new Brackish dataset with the Open Images categories, see Table 3, and the Brackish categories'
C_EV: Sec. 5.2/Fig. 6: 'The AP is plotted against a prediction confidence threshold ... a low confidence threshold of 0.01 is chosen'
E_EV: Sec. 5.2: 'The AP and the AP50, which are the primary metrics of MS COCO and PASCAL VOC, are used as performance indicators.'
NOTE: Dataset paper; turbidity only described in words despite title ('varying visibility'); no stratified results by turbidity. Depth (~9 m) and LED lighting (1900 lumens, always on) reported. Random frame split 80/10/10 of frames from 89 clips -> D_ALL N; authors note near-identical starfish annotations but do not frame it as leakage. FPS: camera spec 'up to 30 fps' only, coded NR. PRE: YOLOv2 ImageNet + NOAA fish fine-tuning; YOLOv3 pre-trained on Open Images (no matching option) — coded ImageNet. Includes non-fish classes; fish only coarsely as big/small.
